header: The State. Versus Muhammad Umar Satti alias Commando.
Muhammad Umar Satti alias Commando. Versus The State, etc.
body: Appellant by: Barrister Osama Amin Qazi Advocate.
State by: Malik Muhammad Latif, APG with Sohaib S.I.
Complainant by:- In person.

SYED FARHAD ALI SHAH, J. Appellant (Muhammad Umar Satti alias Commando) along with his co-accused Abdul Rehman Kiayani, Muhammad Ali alias Ramzan Pathan and Waji-ul-Hassan (since acquitted) has been tried by the trial Court in case FIR No.2156 dated 17.05.2023 offences under Sections 302/324/337-F(vi)/337- H(ii)/148/149 PPC, Police Station Sadiqabad, District Rawalpindiwas convicted and sentenced vide judgement dated 22.09.2026 as under: - Muhammad Umar Satti alias Commando (Appellant) u/s 302 (b) PPC Sentenced to DEATH as Tazir for committing Qatl-i- Amd of Ahmed Ziam (deceased) with compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- payable to legal heirs of deceased u/s 544-A Cr.P.C., (recoverable as arrears of land revenue). u/s 324 PPC Sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for ten years with fine of Rs.200,000/- and in default whereof to further undergo simple imprisonment for six months.
u/s 337-F(vi) PPC Sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for seven years and to pay DAMAN Rs.200,000/- to injured PW/complainant (Ammar Altaf Satti).

2. Appellant has filed this Criminal Appeal against his conviction and the trial Court has sent Murder Reference for confirmation of his death sentence or otherwise, which are being decided through this single judgment.
3. Heard. Record perused.

4. Ahmed Ziam was done to death whereas Ammar Altaf Satti sustained firearm injuries during the occurrence took place on the road on 17.05.2023 at 07:50 p.m., whereafter FIR was lodged on the same night at 11:30 p.m. on the complaint of his brother Ammar Altaf Satti who while claiming himself to be the eyewitness of the occurrence stated in his statement before the trial Court as under:- “Stated that on 17.05.2023 I alongwith my younger brother Ahmed Ziam was present in my house. Umer Satti accused present in court made a telephonic call to my brother Ahmed Ziam and asked him to come to his house alongwith his brother for compromise. I alongwith my younger brother Ahmed Ziam after telling my father left for his house on motorcycle towards Jahaz ground Noora road Rawalpindi. My father Altaf Hussain alongwith Nadeem Aurangzaib also came behind us on their car. At about 7:50 p.m when I alongwith my brother reached Noora road, Rawalpindi the accused persons namely Umer Satti armed with pistol, Raja Farrukh alias Farry armed with pistol (since P.O), Waji ul Hassan armed with pistol, Abdul Rehman Kiani armed with pistol, Muhammad Ali alias Ramzan Pathan armed with pistol (accuse persons identified as present in court) and Ali Jan armed with pistol (since P.O) were present and we saw them in the light of street lights. The accused persons started quarrelling with us during talks and during this quarrel the qameez of my younger brother Ahmed Ziam since deceased was torn out. Meanwhile, Umer Satti accused made a lalkara and asked his co-accused persons that both of us should not go back alive. Umer Satti took out pistol from his dub and made a fire shot with the intention to murder my brother Ahmed Ziam that hit him on right thigh. After that second fire shot was made by Umer Satti accused at my brother that hit him beneath of belly button and my brother fell down on the ground in injured condition. Accused Farrukh alias Farry made fire shot at my brother that hit him on his back. I came forward to attend my brother and accused Umer Satti made fire with his pistol at me that hit me on my left thigh. After that Raja Farrukh made fire shot with his pistol at me that hit me on my right leg. The unknown accused persons also made fire shots at me due to which I became injured and fell down on the ground. Meanwhile my father and my cousin Nadeem Aurangzaib raise hue and cry and due to said hue and cry accused persons fled away from the crime scene by brandishing their respective weapons. My younger brother Ahmed Ziam succumbed to injuries at the spot whereas I sustained serious injuries. The occurrence was witnessed by me, my father and Nadeem Aurangzaib in the light of street lights. My father and my cousin Nadeem Aurangzaib shifted me and the dead body of my younger brother to the hospital. The accused persons have murdered my younger brother and injured me with the intention to murder me, with common intention an object.”
5. Altaf Hussain Satti PW-17 while appearing before the trial Court has reiterated the same story.

6. Both the abovementioned witnesses were crossexamined at length but their evidence could not be shaken during the process of cross-examination. They corroborated one another on all material aspects of the case. They have also established their presence at the time of occurrence at the place of occurrence with their stated reasons. Their evidence is straight forward, trustworthy, confidence inspiring and cannot be discarded mere on probabilities.

7. The discrepancies in the statements of the PWs pointed out by learned counsel for the appellant are minor and general in nature, occur in every case when witnesses (who are human beings) are cross-examined at later stage as in present case, are not fatal to the prosecution case.

8. Acquittal of co-accused (Abdul Rehman Kiayani, Muhammad Ali alias Ramzan Pathan and Waji-ul-Hassan) with different role in earlier trial is also not fatal to the prosecution case. (2020 SCMR 1414) “Javed Ishfaq Vs. The State”. The argument advanced by learned counsel for the appellant to the effect that Waji-ul-Hassan (co-accused), who was not nominated in the FIR but was subsequently implicated through a supplementary statement and attributed an injury on the person of the injured, has been acquitted by disbelieving the testimony of the injured, thereby entitling the appellant to acquittal as well, is devoid of force. It is well settled that a supplementary statement recorded during investigation under section 161, Cr.P.C. does not carry the status of an FIR nor can it be treated as part thereof. The subsequent introduction of the name of an accused, who was not nominated in the initial version, is a circumstance which calls for cautious scrutiny, as the possibility of deliberation, consultation or improvement cannot be ruled out, particularly where no plausible explanation is furnished for his earlier omission. The Hon’ble Supreme Court of Pakistan in Falak Sher alias Sheru v. The State (1995 SCMR 1350) and Akhtar Ali and others v. The State (2008 SCMR 6) has considered the legal worth of subsequent nomination through a supplementary statement and the effect of improvements in the prosecution version. Nevertheless, it cannot be laid down as an inflexible proposition that every accused nominated through a supplementary statement is entitled to acquittal merely on that account. Equally, the acquittal of a coaccused subsequently nominated in the case does not, by itself, furnish a valid ground for extending the same benefit to the appellant. The evidence against each accused is required to be assessed independently in the light of his specific role, the nature of the accusation and the material available on record. The rule of consistency cannot be invoked mechanically, particularly where the appellant was nominated in the promptly lodged FIR and a specific role was attributed to him therein, whereas the involvement of the acquitted co-accused was introduced subsequently through an improved version. Thus, unless the evidence against the appellant suffers from the same infirmity or is otherwise rendered doubtful, the acquittal of Waji-ul-Hassan would not, by itself, entitle the appellant to the same relief.
9. Both the parties were previously known to each other, so there is no question of misidentify of the appellant leaving the actual culprit scot free.

10. Medical evidence has been furnished by Dr. Zia ur Rehman PW-9 who conducted medical examination on the person of Ammar Altaf Satti/injured , who observed firearm injuries on his person attributed to the appellant, and Dr. Syed Shujaat Hussain, CMO PW-5 , who conducted post-mortem examination on the dead body of Ahmed Ziam (deceased) and during post-mortem examination observed firearm injuries on his person attributed to the appellant and others, which were antemortem in nature and were sufficient to cause death in ordinary course of nature, therefore, the medical evidence has fully supported the ocular account discussed above.
11. Motive of the occurrence was quarrel between Ahmed Ziam (deceased) and accused but solid evidence in this respect has not been produced, which is not believable.

12. Shahzad Akbar PW-2 stated before the trial Court that on 29.10.2023, Muhammad Umar Satti alias Commando (appellant) during interrogation disclosed and got recovered pistol .30-bore from the residential room of his house. Rough site plan of place of recovery does not show the house of this witness around the place of recovery. I.O. has not joined any independent person from the locality to witness the recovery proceedings, which are not believable. (2008 SCMR 1064) “Ghulam Akbar and another Vs. The State”.

13. Appellant has denied his involvement in this case in his statement recorded u/s 342 Cr.P.C. and stated that he is innocent and has falsely been involved in this case. He has neither opted to appear as witness u/s 340 (2) Cr.P.C. nor produced any defence evidence in support of his defence plea, which is not believable.

14. In view of above, if evidence of motive and recovery is excluded from consideration, even then prosecution has proved its case beyond shadow of doubt against appellant through the evidence discussed above.

15. Coming to the quantum of sentence, we have noted some mitigating circumstances i.e. firstly, recovery of pistol .30-bore has been disbelieved by us with the reasons mentioned in para 12 of this judgment secondly, co-accused (Abdul Rehman Kiayani, Muhammad Ali alias Ramzan Pathan and Waji-ul-Hassan) have been acquitted by the trial Court through the impugned judgment and thirdly, motive story has also been disbelieved by us with the reasons mentioned in para 11 of this judgment. It is not determinable in this case as to what was the real cause of occurrence and as to what had actually happened immediately before the occurrence which resulted into present unfortunate incident. (2014 SCMR 1227) “Zafar Iqbal and others Vs. The State”.

16. Considering above, conviction of appellant (Muhammad Umar Satti alias Commando) in offence under Section 302(b) PPC for committing the murder of Ahmed Ziam (deceased) is maintained but his sentence is altered from death to imprisonment for life. The compensation and sentence in default whereof awarded by the trial Court are also maintained. Conviction and sentences of the appellant awarded by the trial Court on other heads are also maintained. Sentences of the appellant shall run concurrently with benefit of Section 382-B Cr.P.C.

17. Consequently, with the above said modification in the impugned judgment, instant Criminal Appeal filed by the appellant (Muhammad Umar Satti alias Commando) is hereby dismissed. Murder Reference is answered in NEGATIVE and death sentence of Muhammad Umar Satti alias Commando (appellant) is NOT CONFIRMED.

18. Before parting with this judgment, it is observed that co-accused Raja Farrukh alias Farry and Ali Jan (since POs) shall be decided by the trial court, on its own merits, without being influenced from this judgment, on their arrest.
(SADAQAT ALI KHAN)
Judge (SYED FARHAD ALI SHAH)
